title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Mineral Resource Compensation Fees Should Be Paid for Sand Mining in River Courses

articles.content_en:
Reply is given as follows.

Annex:
The Higher People’s Court of Hunan Province
Request for Instructions on Whether the Collection of Mineral Resources Compensation Fees Should Be Imposed for Sand Mining in River Channels

May 15, 1995 Xiang Gao Fa Xing [1995] No. 2

To the Supreme People’s Court:

In hearing the case of Hengyang Sand and Stone Company v. Hengyang Municipal Bureau of Mineral Resources Administration concerning the collection of mineral resources compensation fees, our province encountered issues regarding the application of the Provisions on the Administration of the Collection of Mineral Resources Compensation Fees, Document Guo Xun [1993] No. 76 of the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters, and the Summary of the Meeting of the National Leading Group for Rectifying “Three Arbitrary Charges”. We hereby request instructions as follows:

Article 2 of the Provisions on the Administration of the Collection of Mineral Resources Compensation Fees promulgated by the State Council provides: “Anyone who exploits mineral resources within the territory of the People’s Republic of China and other sea areas under its jurisdiction shall pay mineral resources compensation fees in accordance with these Provisions; where laws and administrative regulations provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.” According to the legislative interpretation by the Ministry of Geology and Mineral Resources in Document Di Han [1994] No. 186, “sand and gravel in river channels are mineral resources, belonging to non-metallic minerals; those engaged in mining activities in river channels shall pay mineral resources compensation fees.” However, the Notice of the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters, Document Guo Xun [1993] No. 6, explicitly states: “Sand and gravel in river channels are not mineral resources.” The Summary of the Meeting of the National Leading Group for Rectifying “Three Arbitrary Charges” determined: “Both the water conservancy department and the geological and mineral department charge management fees for sand mining in river channels, resulting in duplicate charges; it is decided that only the water conservancy department shall collect management fees for sand mining in river channels.” We understand that if the document of the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters and the Summary of the Meeting of the National Leading Group for Rectifying “Three Arbitrary Charges” of the State Council have the effect of administrative regulations, then for sand mining in river channels, the geological and mineral department may not collect mineral resources compensation fees, and only the water conservancy department may collect management fees for river channel sand mining. As we are uncertain about how to confirm the validity of Document Guo Xun [1993] No. 6 and the Summary of the Meeting of the National Leading Group for Rectifying “Three Arbitrary Charges” of the State Council, we hereby request the Supreme People’s Court to submit this matter to the State Council for interpretation.
